greeting: Good morning, Zuhair. Victoria votes on Saturday, so here's a calm catch-up before polling day.

lead.headline: Late Coalition costings put sewerage lease at the centre of Victoria's election finale
lead.summary: The Coalition released its costings two days before polling day, after about 2 million people had already voted. They include 90-year leases over part of the sewerage network, which Opposition Leader Jess Wilson says is not privatisation, and cuts or delays to some level crossing removals. Voting closes at 6pm on Saturday.

stories.headline: Study finds many AI models too willing to help with illegal requests
stories.summary: Published in Nature Communications on 20 November, this study tested ten widely used language models in Chinese and US legal settings. Most gave safe responses less than 75% of the time in the Chinese setting and less than 70% in the US one.

stories.headline: Brain-like AI vision models may not work as much like brains as they seem
stories.summary: This Nature Machine Intelligence paper from March, back in the news last week, flips the usual test and asks whether brain activity can predict what is inside a model. Many internal features could not be predicted, even in models that predict brain responses well.

stories.headline: Networks of AI agents show human-like patterns of polarisation
stories.summary: This Nature Communications paper, dated 6 November, studied language model agents that form opinions while communicating with each other. Their collective views showed behaviour patterns consistent with those seen in human studies.

stories.headline: Switzerland says AI agents were used in five cyberattacks
stories.summary: The federal cybersecurity office says the recent attacks targeted companies and critical infrastructure, including power, water and telecom providers, and systems were compromised in four cases. It did not say who was responsible.

stories.headline: Nvidia reportedly pauses AI server shipments to four South-East Asian countries
stories.summary: Citing a Financial Times report, The National says Nvidia told server makers to stop shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after new US export rules. It is unclear whether the halt is temporary.

stories.headline: Bank of England warns about the way the AI boom is being financed
stories.summary: Its stability report says increasingly complex and circular funding makes it more likely that market stress will spread. Bank staff put big cloud companies' total potential exposure at just over US$4 trillion.

stories.headline: Pauline Hanson joins One Nation's campaign push on election eve
stories.summary: Hanson led a campaign bus across Melbourne on the final day before the vote. The ABC's live blog also covers the last-day argument over the major parties' plans.

stories.headline: Erin Patterson asks the High Court to hear her appeal
stories.summary: Lawyers for the triple murderer applied on the last day allowed, after the Court of Appeal rejected all her grounds. The High Court must first decide whether to hear the case, which could take months.

stories.headline: Police find part of a stolen Melbourne Cup in Elsternwick
stories.summary: Detectives seized the top of one of the 2003 cups and about 2kg of melted gold. Two men have been charged and are due back in court next year.

stories.headline: Summer outlook flags higher fire risk in parts of Victoria
stories.summary: Bushfire and grassfire risk is expected to be raised from January in the north, west and far East Gippsland. Authorities are urging people to prepare now, including for floods and thunderstorm asthma.

stories.headline: Two Italian workers killed in drone strike on Kuwait
stories.summary: Italy says the two technicians died when drones hit an air-defence surveillance station. Kuwait described the attack as Iranian, while Iran denies any involvement.

stories.headline: Zelenskyy warns another major Russian strike is coming
stories.summary: Citing intelligence, Ukraine's president says Russia is preparing a large attack on power, logistics and other critical services. The warning came as a US envoy said peace talks were deadlocked over territory.

thought: Democracy is a good time to read the fine print, and a good day to have your say.
